cards.card: SriLankan Airlines Platinum American Express Card

note: Sri Lanka's largest private banks are Commercial Bank, Hatton National Bank, Sampath and Seylan (with the state Bank of Ceylon and People's Bank). Commercial Bank's and HNB's sites didn't answer this research (no connection, 2026-10-30) and Sampath's card page shows a captcha, which this research doesn't pass; so Seylan Bank, this file's bank since 2026-10-29, is written alone. Seylan's Mastercard Freedom page (read again 2026-10-30): 28.00% a year from 1 July 2026; no fee but a maintenance charge of 1,500 rupees in a billing cycle with less than 10,000 rupees spent (kept, as written since 2026-10-29, as a monthly fee waived by that spending); up to 51 days free of interest; on spending abroad an added amount of at least 4.50%, written as 4.50%. Seylan's service charges page (read 2026-10-30), each credit card's table: 28.00% a year from 1 July 2026; the annual fee and the joining fee (written as the issue fee): Visa Platinum 3,500 and 2,750 rupees, Visa Gold 2,500 and 1,250, World Mastercard and Visa Signature 6,000 and 2,750 (marked with an asterisk whose note wasn't found), Visa Infinite free; up to 51 days free of interest on purchases when paid in full; a late payment 2,000 rupees; over the limit 1,950 rupees (from 9 March 2026); a cash advance 700 rupees or 4.00%, whichever is higher; a cheque returned 'refer to drawer' 2,000 rupees (Platinum and Gold; other reasons 1,000, not written); spending abroad at least 4.50% added (the 3.5% on overseas spending billed in rupees isn't written). The SMS alert fee of 500 a year, the paper-statement fee and the corporate and cash-backed cards aren't written. No minimum payment is stated. Wave 4 (2026-10-30): Nations Trust Bank, the American Express issuer and a large card issuer, and Pan Asia Bank, whose full tariff prices its Mastercard credit cards, are added; Commercial Bank's and Bank of Ceylon's sites answer 403, HNB's and Cargills Bank's a captcha, NDB's and Standard Chartered Sri Lanka's Incapsula's block, and HSBC Sri Lanka's card page 404 (2026-10-30). Nations Trust Bank's credit card fees and charges (effective from 2 July 2026; a PDF whose tables are images, read by eye on 2026-10-30): the primary card's joining fee (written as the issue fee) and annual fee, American Express Explorer none and 22,500 rupees, SriLankan Airlines Platinum American Express none and 15,000, Centurion Platinum none and 7,500, Gold 1,250 and 5,000, Magnet 500 and 5,000, Blue 300 and 2,500, MasterCard World 1,250 and 6,000, MasterCard Platinum 1,250 and 2,500; finance charges and cash advance interest 2.25% a month (27% a year) on the Explorer and 2.33% a month (28% a year) on the others, written as monthly rates; a local cash advance 1,250 rupees plus 5% of the amount (abroad 5 US dollars plus 5%, not written); up to 50 days of credit on new purchases (20 at least), written as 50; the minimum amount due 4% or 250 rupees, whichever is higher; a late payment 2,000 rupees; over the limit 2,000. The Private Banking Mastercard (for Private Banking clients), the corporate and business cards, and the foreign-transaction fee (on pages not read) aren't written. Pan Asia Bank's full tariff (as at 4 September 2026, read 2026-10-30, its credit card table checked by eye against the rendered page): no joining fee; the primary card's annual fee, Gold 4,000 rupees, Black 5,000, World 6,500 with its first year free; interest 26% a year on purchases and cash advances; a cash advance 5% or 1,000 rupees, whichever is higher; a late payment 2,000; over the limit 1,500 (none on the World); a returned cheque 500 (none on the World); a forex markup of 4%. The Privilege Club card isn't written; no minimum payment or grace period is stated. Wave 5 (2026-10-30), minimum payments: Seylan Bank's examples on interest calculation for its credit cards (dated 12 October 2026, read 2026-10-30) state that the minimum payment is 3% of the closing balance (its cardholder agreement of August 2023 defines the minimum without a figure), written on its six cards as 3%. No minimum payment is published for Pan Asia Bank's three cards; tried: its tariff of 4 September 2026 and its Gold, Black and World card pages (which give the late fee and a standing order of 5% to 100% of the balance, not the minimum), a web search, and archive.org (a 2024 snapshot of the Gold page exists, but web.archive.org is refused by this research's network).
